rubric.title: The 5-step answer formula
rubric.instruction: Use it for every subjective question.

steps.name: WHY
steps.check: why it exists / what problem it solves

steps.name: COMPARE
steps.check: a small table vs the "other" option (A vs B)

steps.name: EXAMPLE
steps.check: a real or lecture example (Big Billion Days, ATM verifyPIN, YouTube clusters...)

steps.name: CONCLUDE
steps.check: answer the scenario: "So for this case, choose ... because ..."

workedExample.prompt: A start-up expects traffic to jump 50× during IPL. Should it use VMs or containers? Justify.

steps.text: Define: a VM is a full virtual computer with its own guest OS, running on a hypervisor. A container packages an app and its libraries and shares the host kernel.
Why: both let one physical machine run many isolated workloads, so resources are used efficiently.
Compare (a mini table): isolation (OS-level vs process-level), size (GBs vs MBs), startup (minutes vs seconds), OS choice (any vs the same kernel).
Example: Netflix runs hundreds of microservice containers on Kubernetes, which scale out in seconds.

Conclude: for a sudden IPL spike, use containers (Docker + Kubernetes) on cloud VMs with elastic auto-scaling, because they start in seconds and are cheap to add. Keep VMs underneath for isolation between tenants.

top25.question: Compare von Neumann, Harvard and modified Harvard. Which do modern CPUs use and why?
top25.outline: Unified vs split at all levels vs split L1 + unified below. von Neumann bottleneck (no pipelining). Harvard can't balance or modify instructions. Modified Harvard is used today. Draw a diagram

top25.question: How does a multi-core system handle an L1 miss? Look-through vs look-aside; write-update vs write-invalidate
top25.outline: Check the other cores' L1s first (coherence), then L2/L3/RAM. Look-through = sequential (standard); look-aside = parallel + cancel. Invalidate for many writes, update for few

top25.question: Explain spatial and temporal locality using a code snippet (the Fibonacci array)
top25.outline: i = temporal (every iteration); array A = spatial (sequential). Caches move blocks. 80/20 rule. Row-major loop order

top25.question: SRAM vs DRAM; NAND vs NOR; HDD vs SSD
top25.outline: Tables: refresh, speed, cell size, OS-transparent or not; density vs execute-in-place; seek + rotation vs constant access, wear levelling, slow writes

top25.question: Block vs character devices. Why a buffer cache?
top25.outline: 1 I/O vs 1024 I/Os per 1 KB. The buffer cache keeps the block in RAM, so later bytes are memory reads

top25.question: Explain the OS as a resource manager, and the path user → shell → system call → kernel → hardware
top25.outline: Layers, privileged I/O (dual mode), why a CLI suits remote work, everything is a file

top25.question: A scenario on hard vs soft links (delete the original, then what happens?)
top25.outline: Same inode, survives deletion, no directories, same filesystem vs a path that can dangle, works across filesystems and for directories. Use ls -i

top25.question: Write a pipeline to find the top 5 error IPs in a log file
top25.outline: grep ERROR → cut -d' ' -f1 → sort → uniq -c → sort -nr → head -5 (joined with pipes; full command in Chapter 3). Explain each stage; pipes are FIFO

top25.question: Write a shell script with argument validation (prime, Fibonacci, file type, second largest)
top25.outline: Shebang, $# check, range check, loop with expr or $(( )) , output. See the Week 4 quiz solutions

top25.question: Trace a fork() program. Explain the process states, zombies and orphans
top25.outline: 2ⁿ processes; 0 in the child and the PID in the parent; the 5-state diagram; zombie until wait; orphans go to init (PID 1)

top25.question: Threads vs processes: what's shared and what's private? Thread pools?
top25.outline: Shared: code, data, heap, files, signal handlers, CWD. Private: stack, registers, signal mask. Pools give a bound and avoid creation cost

top25.question: Race condition → critical section → semaphore; producer–consumer
top25.outline: count++ = load/add/store. 3 requirements. mutex = 1 , empty = n , full = 0 and the order of waits

top25.question: Abstraction vs virtualisation. Process VM vs system VM, with examples
top25.outline: Hide vs change details. JVM, debugger, emulator vs VMware GSX, VirtualBox. Isolation

top25.question: VMs vs containers. When to use which? (Weeks 6 and 12)
top25.outline: The table plus the knife/cutter analogy; banking, legacy, mixed OS vs microservices; containers on VMs in the cloud

top25.question: HLL VMs and K+N; Python venv
top25.outline: Bytecode lets 100 languages × 10 machines need 110 compilers instead of 1000. venv isolates packages per project

top25.question: A Git team workflow and merge-conflict scenario. Centralised vs distributed
top25.outline: clone → branch → add → commit → pull → push → PR. A conflict on the same line needs a human. SVN vs Git table

top25.question: Compiler vs interpreter; how Python runs; JIT
top25.outline: Whole program vs line by line. .py → .pyc bytecode → PVM. JIT compiles hot code at run time

top25.question: Error types, plus how you'd profile and debug a slow, wrong program
top25.outline: Compile-time, run-time and logical errors. pylint/radon (static) vs cProfile/memory_profiler (dynamic). Breakpoints, step over/into, watch. The len-1 bug

top25.question: CPU vs GPU, and the host–device workflow
top25.outline: Few powerful cores vs thousands of simple ones. The 4 steps. The PCIe bottleneck. The physician/specialist analogy

top25.question: Thread/block/grid/warp calculations; SIMT and divergence
top25.outline: Warps = threads ÷ 32. A block is set by the programmer, a warp by the hardware. Divergence serialises the paths

top25.question: The GPU memory hierarchy and tiled matrix multiplication
top25.outline: Cycle table, 1 cycle = 1/f. Tiles in shared memory, reuse, sync, 10×+ faster

top25.question: Why distributed systems? Client–server, RPC, scaling, the 4 server attributes
top25.outline: Data, compute, spikes, fault tolerance. ATM RPC. Horizontal vs vertical + a load balancer. Throughput, response time, reliability, availability

top25.question: Partitioning vs replication; HDFS; a search-engine back end
top25.outline: Split vs copy, the hybrid. 128 MB × 3 (storage calculation). Parallel query across partitions

top25.question: Cloud: technical and business needs; Type 1 vs Type 2; elasticity vs scalability; multi-tenancy
top25.outline: Elasticity, global reach, availability; pay-as-you-go. ESXi vs VirtualBox. Automatic up and down. Netflix and Airbnb on AWS

top25.question: Mobile constraints, SoC, Android stack, the phone as a client
top25.outline: Battery, thermal, RAM, ARM big.LITTLE, NPU/ISP/DSP. Apps → framework → ART → HAL → kernel. REST/JSON/HTTPS, retry, cache, async
